page: Microsoft Azure D96alds_v6 is an x86_64 compute instance belonging to the Daldv6 family, running on dedicated AMD processors under Microsoft Hyper-V. It is provisioned with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 192 GB of memory, representing a compact 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU allocation. The instance does not feature graphics processing units or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Local storage is a defining characteristic of the D96alds_v6, which is equipped with 5,670 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD capacity. This expansive local disk layer facilitates high-throughput scratch space and rapid ephemeral read-write operations. Additionally, the instance is capable of attaching Premium Storage volumes to meet enterprise durability and persistent disk requirements.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the D96alds_v6 is its reduced memory footprint compared to traditional general-purpose virtual machines. By allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU instead of higher standard allocations, it optimizes host resource density and cost efficiency for processing tasks that do not depend on massive working sets in RAM. The provision of substantial local NVMe storage directly offsets the lean memory by enabling low-latency disk-backed buffering and caching.

Given its heavy multi-core CPU capacity and large local NVMe volume, Microsoft Azure D96alds_v6 is well suited for parallel compilation, continuous integration and deployment workers, video rendering, extract-transform-load routines, and distributed computational jobs that generate large temporary datasets.
description: Microsoft Azure D96alds_v6 is a high-density x86_64 virtual machine powered by AMD processors and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The server supplies 96 dedicated vCPUs paired with 192 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. For high-speed temporary data persistence, the instance integrates 5,670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for Premium Storage tiers. It contains no attached GPU accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The hardware architecture prioritizes raw CPU concurrency and low-latency storage throughput over expansive memory capacity. This configuration provides a cost-effective operational profile for compute-intensive tasks requiring fast local disk I/O, though the reduced RAM-per-core ratio limits its utility for memory-heavy databases. Microsoft Azure D96alds_v6 is suitable for large-scale build systems, distributed computing nodes, batch processing, video encoding pipelines, and scratchpad data transformations.
